ault.meta: Welcome to Ault. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
ault.welcome: Ault is a small, close-knit agricultural town in Weld County, sitting along US Highway 85 just a few miles north of Eaton and about 12 miles north of Greeley. Founded in 1904, Ault has held onto its farming roots even as the broader Front Range grows up around it. It's the kind of place where Main Street antique shops, a slower rhythm, and open prairie views still define daily life, and where neighbors genuinely know each other. For buyers who want small-town quiet, easy highway access to Greeley and Fort Collins, and land that still feels like Colorado's high plains, Ault offers a slower pace without being far from anything.
ault.things_to_do: Liberty Park is Ault's community park and the site of the town's annual Fall Festival each August. A small strip of local antique and secondhand shops along Main Street draws browsers from around Weld County. Ault also sits along the route east on CO-14 toward Pawnee National Grassland, home to the Pawnee Buttes Trail and some of the best birdwatching in Northern Colorado, roughly an hour's drive from town. Because Ault is very small, residents rely on nearby Eaton (about 6 miles south) for the A.J. Eaton Home and Carriage House Museum and the Eaton Area Community Center, and on Greeley (about 12 miles south) for larger shopping, dining, and entertainment.
ault.restaurants: Ault is small, but it does have a handful of genuine local spots, including a local cafe and pizza shop on Main Street. For a wider selection, Eaton (6 miles) and Greeley (12 miles) have considerably more dining options.
ault.dog_parks: Ault does not have its own dog park. The nearest real off-leash options are Rover Run Dog Park in Greeley (about 12 miles) or Poudre Pooch Park in Windsor (about 16 miles). Liberty Park in Ault is a fine leashed-dog spot for a local walk.
ault.hikes: The Pawnee Buttes Trail in Pawnee National Grassland is a roughly 2-mile trail to the base of the first Pawnee Butte, with unique rock formations, reached via CO-14 east of Ault. The Great Western Trail, about a 10-15 minute drive south, and the Poudre River Trail, about 15-20 minutes south, are the closest longer trails.
ault.commute: About 12 miles / roughly 15-18 minutes to Greeley via US-85, Ault's nearest job center.
ault.relocate_extra: Ault is a classic agricultural/ranching plains town — real estate leans toward larger lots on well-and-septic with agricultural zoning just outside town limits, appealing to buyers wanting acreage and rural character within a short drive of Greeley.

berthoud.meta: Welcome to Berthoud. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
berthoud.welcome: Berthoud, Colorado, is a picturesque town often called the “Garden Spot of Colorado” for its lush landscapes and tree-lined streets. Nestled between Longmont and Loveland, it combines small-town charm with stunning views of the Rocky Mountains. Known for its tight-knit community, Berthoud offers a welcoming atmosphere, historic character, and a love for outdoor living, making it a truly special place to call home.
berthoud.things_to_do: Visit City Star Brewing to enjoy handcrafted beers in a welcoming atmosphere. The brewery often hosts live music and community events, making it a local favorite. Explore Carter Lake Reservoir, a popular spot for boating, fishing, camping, and hiking. The surrounding trails offer scenic views and opportunities for wildlife observation. Delve into local history at the Little Thompson Valley Pioneer Museum, which showcases artifacts and exhibits detailing Berthoud's rich heritage. Experience wine tasting at Blue Mountain Vineyards, where you can sample a variety of locally produced wines in a picturesque setting. For astronomy enthusiasts, the Little Thompson Observatory offers public viewing nights, providing a chance to explore the night sky through powerful telescopes.
berthoud.restaurants: Berthoud's Main Street has a growing food scene anchored by cozy local spots. Joyful Brews is a beloved coffee shop just off Main Street, while Trailhead Cafe and Cornerstone Cafe are popular for hearty breakfasts and lunch. For dinner, Berthoud Pizza Company is a longtime local favorite for pizza and fresh salads.
berthoud.dog_parks: The town operates the Berthoud Dog Park at 202 10th St., a fully fenced, double-gated off-leash area. Carter Lake Reservoir, just west of town, also allows leashed dogs on its trails and shorelines.
berthoud.hikes: The Carter Lake Reservoir Sundance Trail is the standout — a scenic, mostly flat, roughly 6-mile out-and-back along the lake's west shore (a park entrance fee applies). For a shorter outing close to town, Pinewood Reservoir near Ramsay-Shockey Open Space offers additional lake-view hiking a short drive from Berthoud.
berthoud.commute: About 7 miles (12 min) to Loveland, 20 miles (37 min) to Fort Collins via US-287, and roughly 46 miles (about 56 min) to Denver via I-25.
berthoud.relocate_extra: Berthoud is one of the faster-growing towns in Larimer County, with active master-planned new-home communities such as Berthoud Harvest and Farmstead adding significant new-construction inventory to a historically small-town market.

boulder.meta: Welcome to Boulder. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
boulder.welcome: Boulder, Colorado, is a vibrant city renowned for its stunning natural beauty, progressive culture, and outdoor lifestyle. Nestled at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains, Boulder offers endless recreational opportunities, a thriving arts scene, and a commitment to sustainability. With its dynamic community, world-class dining, and picturesque surroundings, Boulder is a truly unique place to live and explore.
boulder.things_to_do: Explore the Pearl Street Mall, a vibrant pedestrian area featuring a mix of local shops, restaurants, and street performers. It's an ideal spot for shopping, dining, and soaking in the local culture. Hike the iconic Flatirons, the distinctive rock formations that are a symbol of Boulder. Numerous trails cater to various skill levels, offering breathtaking views of the city and surrounding areas. Visit Chautauqua Park, a historic area that provides access to hiking trails, cultural events, and the Chautauqua Dining Hall. It's a perfect place to experience both nature and Boulder's community events. Experience local produce and artisan goods at the Boulder Farmers Market, held weekly and offering a variety of fresh foods, crafts, and live music. It's a great way to engage with the local community and enjoy fresh, local products. Boulder Museum of Contemporary Art (BMoCA) Explore contemporary art exhibits at the Boulder Museum of Contemporary Art, which showcases innovative artworks and hosts various cultural events throughout the year.
boulder.restaurants: Frasca Food and Wine is a nationally recognized spot for refined Northern Italian cuisine and an exceptional wine list. For a splurge with a view, The Flagstaff House perches on Flagstaff Mountain with panoramic city views. Locals swear by The Sink, a beloved century-old diner near CU Boulder famous for its burgers, and Illegal Pete's is a go-to for burritos after a hike.
boulder.dog_parks: Boulder is highly dog-friendly, with several designated off-leash areas managed by the city, including the Foothills Community Park Dog Park and the Howard Heuston Off-Leash Dog Area. Boulder also allows leash-free hiking with a Voice & Sight tag on many Open Space and Mountain Parks (OSMP) trails.
boulder.hikes: The Chautauqua Trail up to the First and Second Flatirons Loop is the classic Boulder hike, climbing right from Chautauqua Park into the iconic red-rock formations. The Royal Arch Trail, also starting at Chautauqua, is a steeper climb rewarded by a natural rock arch, and Mount Sanitas near downtown is a favorite steep loop for locals.
boulder.commute: About 33 miles / roughly 48 minutes to Loveland via US-36 and CO-119.
boulder.relocate_extra: Boulder's market is tight and ultra-premium: median single-family price runs roughly $1.05M-$1.15M with limited active inventory, and luxury demand concentrates in neighborhoods like Mapleton Hill and Wonderland Hills — partly a result of Boulder's building-height limits and city-owned open space greenbelt constraining new supply.

broomfield-city.meta: Welcome to Broomfield. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
broomfield-city.welcome: Broomfield, Colorado, is a vibrant city offering a perfect mix of small-town charm and modern amenities. Nestled between Denver and Boulder, it boasts stunning open spaces, top-rated schools, and a strong sense of community. With its scenic parks, recreational opportunities, and thriving local economy, Broomfield is an exceptional place to live, work, and play.
broomfield-city.things_to_do: Experience premier shopping at FlatIron Crossing Mall, featuring retail stores, dining options, and the adjacent 14-screen AMC Theatres Flatiron Crossing cinema. Delve into local history at the Broomfield Veterans Memorial Museum. Enjoy outdoor activities at Broomfield County Commons Park, a 300-acre space featuring sports fields, playgrounds, and walking trails. Cool off during the summer months at The Bay Aquatic Park, a family-friendly water park with pools and water slides.
broomfield-city.restaurants: Broomfield's dining scene punches above its size, especially around the Arista district. VINCA at Arista offers upscale European-inspired fine dining, while Hickory & Ash nearby serves a Colorado-centric steakhouse menu. For something more casual, The Burns Pub & Restaurant is a longtime family-owned British pub known for shepherd's pie and live music.
broomfield-city.dog_parks: Broomfield County Commons Dog Park, inside the 300-acre County Commons complex, is fully fenced with separate areas and agility obstacles for dogs of all sizes.
broomfield-city.hikes: The Coal Creek Trail is a 14-mile soft-surface path connecting Broomfield to Superior and Louisville. The Carolyn Holmberg Preserve at Rock Creek Farm offers a quieter network of shorter trails around Stearns Lake, good for bald-eagle spotting, and the Lake Link Trail, an 8.8-mile route, connects Broomfield's eastern and western trail systems.
broomfield-city.school_district: Adams 12 Five Star Schools (primary district for most of the city; a portion of northwest Broomfield falls in Boulder Valley School District Re-2)
broomfield-city.commute: About 42 miles / roughly 45-50 minutes to Loveland, largely via US-287/I-25.
broomfield-city.relocate_extra: Baseline, a large master-planned community between Denver and Boulder, is actively selling new-construction homes from the $500s to $1M+, with a walkable retail district and a new park slated to open in 2027.

brush.meta: Welcome to Brush. Explore Morgan County's second city — 11 miles east of Fort Morgan on I-76, home of the Fourth of July Brush Rodeo, four city parks and a nine-hole municipal golf course.
brush.welcome: Brush sits 11 miles east of Fort Morgan on I-76 — close enough to share Fort Morgan's shopping and hospital runs, far enough to be unmistakably its own town. It's a rodeo-and-fairgrounds community: the Morgan County Fairgrounds are here, not in the county seat. For a town of 5,339 (2020 census) it carries a lot of infrastructure — four city parks, a municipal pool, a nine-hole golf course, its own hospital, and a school district that put its middle and high schools onto one modern campus in 2019. Buyers who start out looking at Fort Morgan very often end up looking here too: same commute, same schools-and-parks checklist, different small town.
brush.things_to_do: The Fourth of July belongs to the Brush Rodeo, held July 2–4 at the Morgan County Fairgrounds on Ellsworth Street — bronc riding, bull riding, barrel racing, mutton bustin', a nightly beer garden, a July 4 parade and fireworks. There have been rodeos in Brush since the early 1900s and an organized rodeo association since the 1950s; it joined the Colorado Professional Rodeo Association in 2005. The rest of the year: the Brush Area Museum & Cultural Center at 314 S. Clayton Street, a walkable historic downtown, nine holes at Petteys Park Golf Course, fishing at Doty Pond in Prairie Trails Park, the municipal pool and playground at Memorial Park, and the Pioneer skate park.
brush.restaurants: Brush punches above its size here. True Grits Steakhouse at 919 Edison Street, right off I-76 exit 90, is the sit-down steak dinner people drive in from other towns for. Drovers Culinary Cafe and Home Plate 2 on Edmunds Street cover breakfast and lunch, and Brush! Emporium & Pizzaporium at 210 Clayton Street is the downtown pizza stop. For anything beyond that it's 11 miles west to Fort Morgan.
brush.dog_parks: Brush has no fenced off-leash dog park, and it's better to say so than to dress it up. The dog-walking here is on-leash: the trail around Doty Pond in Prairie Trails Park (open 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., dogs welcome on leash), plus the paths through Memorial and Petteys parks. The nearest fenced off-leash parks are Fort Morgan's two, 11 miles west.
brush.hikes: Brush Prairie Ponds State Wildlife Area, just outside town, is the real find — about 650 acres of restored wetland and native grassland built out over two decades by Ducks Unlimited and the City of Brush, now a recognized birding hotspot, with a Fort Morgan Canal loop of roughly five miles. Read the rules first, because they're stricter than a city park's: it's a State Wildlife Area, so everyone 16 and older needs a hunting or fishing license or an SWA pass, wildlife viewing is limited to March 1 through August 31 in the posted areas, and the trails are unmarked and unmaintained. For something casual, the pond loop at Prairie Trails Park is in town; Jackson Lake State Park is about 45 minutes northwest, and mountain trailheads are better than two hours away.
brush.commute: About 11 miles and 15 minutes to Fort Morgan on I-76, about 92 miles and an hour and forty minutes to Denver, and about 94 miles to Fort Collins. East Morgan County Hospital is in town on West Edison Street; the larger Colorado Plains Medical Center is in Fort Morgan.
brush.relocate_extra: For families already living in the county, the schools are Brush's practical draw: the district opened the Brush Secondary Campus in 2019, housing Brush Middle School and Brush High School together in one modern building, and enrolls roughly 1,400 students across four schools — small enough that a kid who wants to be on a team is on the team. Housing runs older and more attainable than the Front Range norm, with historic homes near downtown, post-war and newer subdivisions filling in around them, and irrigated acreage in every direction once you're past city limits.

dacono.meta: Welcome to Dacono. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
dacono.welcome: Dacono, Colorado, is a charming and close-knit community offering a relaxed, small-town vibe. Located just off I-25, it provides convenient access to Denver, Boulder, and Northern Colorado. With its scenic surroundings, friendly atmosphere, and growing amenities, Dacono is an inviting place to call home.
dacono.things_to_do: Experience the thrill of live auto racing at the Colorado National Speedway, a premier NASCAR-sanctioned track offering exciting events throughout the racing season. Enjoy outdoor activities at Clem Dufour Park, featuring a splash pad, playgrounds, sports courts, and picnic areas, making it a perfect spot for family outings. Join the community at the annual Dacono Music & Spirits Festival, a one-day event featuring live music, local distilleries, food vendors, and family-friendly activities. For adventure seekers, Blitz Paintball offers an expansive facility with various fields and game scenarios suitable for all skill levels. Test your skills at the IMI Motorsports Complex, which provides kart racing, motocross tracks, and other motorsport activities for enthusiasts.
dacono.restaurants: Dacono is a small town, so dining options are modest and mostly local Mexican spots. El Taco Loco II and Santiago's II Mexican Restaurant are both well-reviewed local favorites, and Wing Shack Dacono is the go-to for wings and casual bar food.
dacono.dog_parks: Dacono itself does not have a dedicated off-leash dog park. The nearest confirmed options are The Boneyard at Reliance Park in Erie or Broomfield County Commons Dog Park, both a 15-20 minute drive.
dacono.hikes: The Firestone Trail, a mostly-paved path connecting Firestone, Frederick, and Dacono, extends into Dacono via its southern Old Railroad Trail segment. St. Vrain State Park, just north in Firestone, offers miles of interconnected, mostly ADA-accessible trails around several ponds.
dacono.school_district: St. Vrain Valley School District RE-1J
dacono.commute: About 28 miles / 39 minutes to Denver via I-25, with direct I-25 access into both Denver and Boulder.
dacono.relocate_extra: Dacono is one of the fastest-growing towns in southern Weld County — population rose over 51% from 2010 to 2020 — driven largely by Denver/Boulder-area buyers seeking more affordable housing.

denver-city.meta: Welcome to Denver. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
denver-city.welcome: Denver, Colorado, is a vibrant urban center celebrated for its rich history, cultural diversity, and breathtaking views of the Rocky Mountains. Known for its lively neighborhoods, thriving business scene, and endless opportunities for recreation and entertainment, Denver City offers an exceptional lifestyle. Whether enjoying the dynamic arts scene or the nearby outdoor adventures, it’s a place where city living meets Colorado’s natural beauty.
denver-city.things_to_do: Explore the Denver Botanic Gardens, featuring a variety of themed gardens, a conservatory, and a sunken amphitheater that hosts various concerts during the summer months. Red Rocks Park and Amphitheatre Experience a concert at the iconic Red Rocks Amphitheatre, known for its natural acoustics and stunning red sandstone formations. The surrounding park offers hiking trails with panoramic views. Visit the Denver Art Museum, renowned for its collection of Native American art and its contemporary exhibits housed in architecturally striking buildings. Discover Union Station, a beautifully restored historic landmark that serves as a transit hub and features restaurants, shops, and the elegant Crawford Hotel. Catch a Colorado Rockies baseball game at Coors Field, known for its classic ballpark atmosphere and views of the Rocky Mountains.
denver-city.restaurants: Gaetano's in the Highlands has served Italian food since the 1940s, making it one of Denver's oldest Italian restaurants. Mezcaleria Alma in LoHi serves CDMX-inspired seafood with an extensive mezcal list, and Hop Alley in RiNo, a Michelin Bib Gourmand winner, offers family-style regional Chinese cooking.
denver-city.dog_parks: Berkeley Lake Dog Park in northwest Denver has separate fenced areas for big and small dogs, and Railyard Dog Park in LoDo — just steps from Union Station — is a favorite for downtown residents.
denver-city.hikes: The Red Rocks and Morrison Slide Trails, right around the amphitheatre, wind past the park's namesake red rock formations. The Green Mountain and Hayden Trail Loop near Golden offers a 3.2-mile easy loop with skyline views back toward downtown Denver.
denver-city.commute: About 51-52 miles to Loveland, entirely on I-25, typically 55-70 minutes depending on metro traffic.
denver-city.relocate_extra: Denver's close-in, walkable neighborhoods (Highlands/LoHi/RiNo) are among the city's highest-demand, highest-premium pockets, appealing to buyers who want dense urban walkability without leaving city limits.

eaton.meta: Welcome to Eaton. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
eaton.welcome: Eaton, Colorado, is a welcoming agricultural town with a rich history and a strong sense of community. Located just north of Greeley, it offers a peaceful, small-town lifestyle surrounded by Colorado’s scenic beauty. Known for its excellent schools and family-friendly atmosphere, Eaton is an ideal place to enjoy a quiet and fulfilling way of life.
eaton.things_to_do: Delve into Eaton's history by visiting the A.J. Eaton Home and Carriage House Museum. Opened in 2017, the Eaton Area Community Center offers a fitness center, indoor track, and leisure pool. Outdoor enthusiasts can explore the Great Western Trail, a 10.5-mile unpaved rail-trail running through Eaton, Severance, and Windsor, ideal for hiking, biking, and horseback riding. Experience local culture at the annual Eaton Days Festival. Discover a unique collection of antique washing machines at the Lee Maxwell Washing Machine Museum, showcasing over 1,800 machines — the world's largest collection of its kind.
eaton.restaurants: Casa Maria Mexican Kitchen & Margaritas is a family-owned favorite for fajitas and margaritas. Route 85 Grill serves casual American fare including weekend breakfast, and McCarty's Restaurant at Eaton Country Club is open to the public for burgers, steaks, and patio dining.
eaton.dog_parks: Eaton itself has no dedicated off-leash dog park. The nearest real option is Rover Run Dog Park in Greeley (about 10 miles) or Poudre Pooch Park in Windsor (about 12 miles). Locally, Eaton Commons Park has walking paths suitable for leashed dogs.
eaton.hikes: The Great Western Trail runs 10.5 miles unpaved through Eaton, Severance, and Windsor. The Poudre River Trail, a 21-mile paved path, runs from Greeley to Windsor about 10 miles south, and the Pawnee Buttes Trail in Pawnee National Grassland is a genuine regional draw about an hour's drive northeast.
eaton.school_district: Weld RE-2 School District (Eaton School District)
eaton.commute: About 9 miles / roughly 15-17 minutes to Greeley via US-85, Eaton's primary job center.
eaton.relocate_extra: Eaton hosts Eaton Days, its signature annual community festival — a good small-town-camaraderie selling point for relocation buyers.

erie.meta: Welcome to Erie. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
erie.welcome: Erie, Colorado, is a vibrant town that blends small-town charm with modern amenities and a lively community spirit. Nestled between Boulder and Denver, Erie offers stunning mountain views, beautiful parks, and top-rated schools. With its thriving downtown, outdoor recreation opportunities, and welcoming atmosphere, Erie provides an exceptional quality of life in Northern Colorado.
erie.things_to_do: Visit the Luvin Arms Animal Sanctuary to meet rescued farm animals through guided tours. Experience seasonal fun at Anderson Farms, known for its 25-acre corn maze, pumpkin patch, and hayrides during the fall season. Enjoy a leisurely walk or fishing at Thomas Reservoir. Spend time at Erie Community Park, a roughly 40-acre space featuring picnic shelters, sports fields, a skatepark, and walking trails. Explore Erie's history at the Wise Homestead Museum, a late 19th-century homestead.
erie.restaurants: 24 Carrot Bistro is a local favorite for weekend brunch, known for its eggs Benedict. The Old Mine is the go-to for comfort food — great pizza and barbecue — and Echo Brewing and Pizzeria rounds things out with house-brewed beer and wood-fired pizza.
erie.dog_parks: Erie has its own dedicated off-leash park: The Boneyard at Reliance Park, a 7.9-acre facility with a double-gated entry and separate fenced areas for large and small dogs.
erie.rec_center: The Erie Community Center (450 Powers St.) is the town's hub for indoor recreation — a full-court gymnasium for basketball and volleyball, an indoor pool with a lazy river and hot tub, racquetball courts, several meeting rooms, and fitness programming, plus the Columbine Lounge for active adults.
erie.hikes: The Erie Forest Trail is a beginner-friendly connector trail through Erie's growing singletrack network. The Coal Creek Trail runs along Erie's edge toward Broomfield and Louisville, and Thomas Reservoir has its own walking loop around the water.
erie.school_district: St. Vrain Valley Schools serves most of Erie (including Erie High School); a portion of town falls in Boulder Valley School District (BVSD) depending on the neighborhood
erie.commute: About 27 miles / 39 minutes to Denver via I-25, and roughly 15-18 miles to Boulder — within a reasonable daily commute of both job centers.
erie.relocate_extra: Erie is one of the southern Weld County towns seeing outsized growth from buyers priced out of Boulder County and metro Denver.
local_faqs: Can you have chickens in Erie, CO?

Yes — the Town of Erie allows backyard chickens, but you need a chicken license from the Town before bringing any chickens onto the property, and the lot must be larger than 5,000 square feet. If the property is in an HOA-governed neighborhood, check with the HOA first — most Erie HOAs prohibit chickens even where the Town itself allows them. For the current hen-count limit and coop setback rules, apply directly through the Town of Erie's Chicken License program at erieco.gov.

estes-park.meta: Welcome to Estes Park. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
estes-park.welcome: Estes Park sits at the eastern gateway to Rocky Mountain National Park, and that single fact shapes everything about living here — the views, the seasons, the economy and the housing market. It is a genuine mountain town rather than a Front Range suburb: elk walk through neighborhoods in the autumn rut, Longs Peak fills the skyline, and the nearest full-service city is a canyon drive away. Buyers here are usually choosing between a primary home with a real commute, a second home, or a short-term rental — three very different purchases in the same small market, which is why local guidance matters more here than almost anywhere else in Larimer County.
estes-park.things_to_do: The Stanley Hotel is the town's landmark — a 140-room Georgian Revival hotel about five miles from the Rocky Mountain National Park entrance, famous for inspiring The Shining, and open for daytime history tours and night tours. Elkhorn Avenue is the walkable heart of downtown, with over 200 shops in Victorian-era buildings. The Estes Park Aerial Tram climbs 2,630 feet to the summit of Prospect Mountain for panoramic views of Longs Peak and the Continental Divide; it runs seasonally, roughly May through the start of November. Trail Ridge Road, the highest continuous paved road in the United States, begins just outside town and closes through the winter.
estes-park.restaurants: Downtown dining is concentrated along Elkhorn Avenue and the Riverwalk, within walking distance of each other — a mix of long-running local kitchens, breweries and taprooms, and the restaurants inside the Stanley Hotel. The practical thing to know is seasonal: hours expand dramatically for the summer and autumn visitor season and contract in the shoulder months, so a place that is packed in September may keep short hours in April.
estes-park.dog_parks: The Lake Estes Trail loop is the everyday walk for most local dog owners — paved, nearly flat, and open year-round. One thing worth knowing before you move here with a dog: Rocky Mountain National Park does not allow dogs on its trails at all. They are permitted only in developed areas such as roadsides, parking lots and campgrounds, so the town's own trails and the surrounding national forest do the work the park cannot.
estes-park.hikes: The Lake Estes Trail is the accessible standout — a paved loop of roughly four miles right in town, with views north to the Lumpy Ridge rock formations. Beyond that, the trailheads of Rocky Mountain National Park are minutes from downtown, and the park now uses a timed-entry reservation system through its busy season, which is worth planning around whether you are visiting or living here.
estes-park.commute: About 40 minutes to Loveland via US-34 through the Big Thompson Canyon — the nearest full-service city — and roughly an hour and a half to Denver. Worth being honest about: the canyon is a beautiful drive and it is also the only practical route east, so winter weather, rockfall closures and summer visitor traffic all land on the same road. Anyone planning a daily Front Range commute should drive it in February before deciding.
estes-park.relocate_extra: Estes Park's market behaves differently from the rest of Larimer County. Inventory is small, a meaningful share of it is second homes and vacation rentals, and short-term rental licensing is limited and regulated by the town — so whether a given property can legally be rented nightly is a question to answer before making an offer, not after. Christine has helped clients buy and sell here many times and knows which streets hold value through the off-season.

firestone.meta: Welcome to Firestone. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
firestone.welcome: Firestone, Colorado, is a vibrant and family-friendly town known for its stunning mountain views and welcoming community. Conveniently located near Longmont and Denver, it offers a perfect mix of small-town charm and modern amenities. With its numerous parks, trails, and recreational opportunities, Firestone provides a high quality of life in the heart of Northern Colorado.
firestone.things_to_do: Enjoy outdoor activities at St. Vrain State Park, which offers opportunities for fishing, camping, and hiking amidst scenic landscapes. Visit Wild Cider to sample a variety of locally crafted ciders in a welcoming atmosphere. Golf enthusiasts can enjoy a round at the Saddleback Golf Club, known for its well-maintained course and beautiful views. Explore a wide selection of books and community programs at the Carbon Valley Regional Library, a great resource for all ages. Relax and play at Neighbors Point Park, a local park offering open spaces and recreational facilities for families and individuals.
firestone.restaurants: Pepper's Fireside Grille is a local American grill, Wild Cider doubles as a dining destination alongside its cidery, and Maya Grill & Cantina covers Mexican fare.
firestone.dog_parks: Firestone's two former dog parks (Settlers Park and Aisik's Meadow) have closed. As of this writing there is no confirmed operating off-leash dog park within Firestone town limits — the nearest options are The Boneyard at Reliance Park in Erie or dog-friendly trails around Longmont, and St. Vrain State Park allows leashed pets on its trails.
firestone.hikes: St. Vrain State Park's roughly 7 miles of trails wind around Blue Heron Reservoir and the park's ponds. The St. Vrain Greenway Trail, a 17.5-mile paved path through nearby Longmont, is about a 15-minute drive away.
firestone.school_district: St. Vrain Valley Schools (includes Firestone Charter Academy, feeds into Frederick High School)
firestone.commute: About 30 miles / 41 minutes to Denver via I-25, and roughly 12-15 minutes to Longmont — dual access to Denver and Boulder-area jobs.
firestone.relocate_extra: Firestone is part of the strongest growth pocket in Weld County (alongside Frederick, Dacono, and Erie), driven by relative affordability compared to Boulder County and metro Denver.

fort-collins.meta: Welcome to Fort Collins. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
fort-collins.welcome: Fort Collins is a vibrant and welcoming city in Northern Colorado, nestled at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains. Known for its thriving craft beer scene, top-rated schools, and abundant outdoor recreation, it offers the perfect balance of small-town charm and big-city amenities. The city features tree-lined streets with historic homes, modern new-build communities, and stunning luxury properties. Neighborhoods like Old Town radiate character and charm, while areas such as Harmony Corridor provide spacious homes with all the conveniences. Whether you’re drawn by its entrepreneurial spirit, world-class biking trails, or vibrant arts scene, Fort Collins is a place where every lifestyle feels at home.
fort-collins.things_to_do: Experience the charm of Old Town Fort Collins, with its preserved 19th-century architecture, unique boutiques, and vibrant dining scene. Old Town is the subject of local lore that its Victorian-era storefronts helped inspire Disneyland's Main Street, U.S.A. — Disney artist Harper Goff, who worked on Main Street's design, grew up in Fort Collins and reportedly showed Walt Disney photos of his hometown, though Disney's most-cited inspiration remains his own hometown of Marceline, Missouri. Engage with interactive exhibits that blend science and history at the Fort Collins Museum of Discovery. Just west of the city, Horsetooth Reservoir offers boating, swimming, fishing, and hiking against stunning mountain vistas. Stroll through the Gardens on Spring Creek, a 12-acre botanical oasis featuring themed gardens and a butterfly house. Enjoy outdoor adventures along the Cache la Poudre River — Colorado's only federally designated National Wild and Scenic River — ideal for whitewater rafting, fishing, and scenic hikes. Tour the New Belgium Brewing Company, one of the nation's largest craft breweries, still headquartered in Fort Collins. Relive the 1980s at Totally 80's Pizza & Museum, where you can enjoy a slice amidst a vast collection of 80s memorabilia.
fort-collins.restaurants: Old Town's dining scene blends comfort food with global flavors. Lucile's Restaurant is a Fort Collins institution for New Orleans-style breakfast, while The Silver Grill Cafe — open since 1933 — is beloved for its towering cinnamon rolls. CooperSmith's Brewpub, right on Old Town Square, is one of the city's original craft breweries and a great people-watching spot.
fort-collins.dog_parks: Fort Collins has several city-run off-leash dog parks. Spring Canyon Community Park (2626 W. Horsetooth Rd.) has the largest, most amenity-rich dog park at the base of the foothills, with tunnels and a doggy pond. Fossil Creek Park and Twin Silo Community Park both offer smaller fenced dog areas in south and southeast Fort Collins.
fort-collins.hikes: Horsetooth Mountain Open Space, just west of the city, offers the iconic climb to Horsetooth Rock plus the seasonal Horsetooth Falls, with 29 miles of connected trails leading into Lory State Park. Closer to town, the paved Poudre River Trail follows the Cache la Poudre through Fort Collins for an easy walk or bike ride.
fort-collins.commute: About 64 miles / roughly 1 hour 17 minutes to Denver via I-25 (longer with typical traffic); about 20 miles / 37 minutes to Berthoud, and roughly 10 miles to Timnath.

fort-lupton.meta: Welcome to Fort Lupton. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
fort-lupton.welcome: Fort Lupton, Colorado, is a historic and welcoming town nestled along the South Platte River. Known for its rich heritage and small-town charm, it offers a peaceful lifestyle with convenient access to Denver and surrounding areas. With its close-knit community, open spaces, and ties to Colorado’s agricultural roots, Fort Lupton is a delightful place to call home.
fort-lupton.things_to_do: Explore the South Platte Valley Historic Park, which features a reconstructed adobe trading post built in 2009 on the site of the original 1830s-40s Fort Lupton, along with other historical buildings. Enjoy a round of golf at the Coyote Creek Golf Course, an 18-hole course suitable for players of all skill levels. Visit the Fort Lupton Museum (open Wednesday-Friday, 9am-3pm) to delve deeper into the city's history. About 20-25 minutes away, Barr Lake State Park offers hiking, bird-watching, and fishing along an 8.8-mile trail that circles the lake.
fort-lupton.restaurants: Wholly Stromboli, a beloved New York-style pizzeria and bar downtown, is often cited as the town's standout eatery, and Santiago's III Mexican Restaurant is a go-to for breakfast burritos.
fort-lupton.dog_parks: Fort Lupton doesn't currently have a dedicated off-leash dog park in town — Pearson Park and Railroad Park are dog-friendly on leash, with walking paths along the South Platte River. For a true off-leash run, the nearest option is Happy Tails Dog Park in Brighton, roughly a 15-minute drive.
fort-lupton.hikes: The Barr Lake Loop / Perimeter Trail (8.8 miles, flat and multi-use) is one of the best easy hikes in the region, about a 20-minute drive from town. Closer to home, Pearson Park's trails wind along the South Platte River through wetlands and open meadows.
fort-lupton.school_district: Weld RE-8 School District, headquartered in Fort Lupton
fort-lupton.commute: About 29 miles / 43 minutes to Denver via US-85 — a direct north-south commute route into the metro area without needing I-25.
fort-lupton.relocate_extra: Fort Lupton has grown more modestly than its neighboring I-25-corridor towns, which may appeal to buyers wanting a quieter, more historic South Platte River town within commuting range of Denver.

fort-morgan.meta: Welcome to Fort Morgan. Explore the Morgan County seat on the South Platte River — Riverside Park, a historic Main Street, and the most in-town amenities anywhere on the I-76 corridor east of Greeley.
fort-morgan.welcome: Fort Morgan is the Morgan County seat and the largest town on I-76 between Greeley and the Nebraska line — 11,597 people at the 2020 census, wrapped around a bend in the South Platte River about 80 miles northeast of Denver. It has what the smaller towns out here don't: its own hospital, Morgan Community College's main campus, a large river park with a summer pool and a campground, two fenced dog parks, and a historic Main Street that still works as the commercial center rather than a preserved streetscape. Buyers come for square footage and land per dollar the Front Range stopped offering years ago. The trade is distance, and it's a real one.
fort-morgan.things_to_do: Riverside Park on the north edge of town is the anchor — ball fields, ponds, a playground, picnic pavilions, a disc golf course, a summer swimming pool with slides and a wading pool, a small city campground with electric hookups, and roughly six miles of nature trails along the South Platte (the outer loop alone runs about 3.4 miles). Downtown, the Fort Morgan Museum at 414 Main Street, inside the library, covers Plains Indian artifacts, the railroad and sugar-beet history that built the town, and a Glenn Miller exhibit — the bandleader grew up here. North of I-76 at exit 80, the 1923 Rainbow Arch Bridge, the only rainbow arch bridge in Colorado and on the National Register of Historic Places, still crosses the river as a pedestrian bridge. In July, the free Bobstock Music Festival takes over Main Street for two days (five stages and 21 bands in 2026), and the Glenn Miller SwingFest brings the big-band programming back each year.
fort-morgan.restaurants: Main Street is where the local dining is: Cables Pub and Grill at 431 Main, the Bun Appetit cafe and coffee counter at 801 Main, and Kukaro Brewing, the closest thing to a craft taproom for a long way in any direction. Chain options cluster on the north end of Main near the interstate. It's an honest small-town food scene rather than a destination one — for a steak-dinner occasion, plenty of locals drive the 11 miles east to True Grits Steakhouse in Brush, and Greeley is an hour away when you want a full restaurant row.
fort-morgan.dog_parks: Fort Morgan has two fenced off-leash dog parks, which is unusual for a town this size: the Fort Morgan Dog Park at Gateway Park, split into separate large- and small-dog sides with agility equipment and waste stations, and a smaller fenced dog park at Fulton Heights Park. Riverside Park's trail network along the river is the everyday leashed walk.
fort-morgan.hikes: This is plains and river country, not foothills, and the honest answer is that the best walking is close to home — Riverside Park's roughly six miles of nature trails along the South Platte, including an outer loop of about 3.4 miles. For a day trip, Jackson Lake State Park is about a half-hour northwest with shoreline walking and sandy beaches, and the Pawnee Pioneer Trails Scenic Byway runs north from town toward the Pawnee National Grassland and the Pawnee Buttes trail — a real hike, but well over an hour of driving to reach it. Mountain trailheads are a two-hour drive west.
fort-morgan.commute: About 83 miles and an hour and a half to Denver on I-76, about 53 miles and an hour to Greeley on US-34, and about 84 miles to Fort Collins. Worth saying plainly: this is a town people commute within rather than out of — Cargill, Leprino Foods, Western Sugar, Colorado Plains Medical Center and Morgan Community College are all inside the city.
fort-morgan.relocate_extra: Fort Morgan's economy is food processing and agriculture, and that shapes the housing market more than any Front Range trend does. Cargill's beef plant is the county's largest employer at roughly 2,100 people, Leprino Foods' cheese plant employs several hundred more, and the Western Sugar Cooperative plant here is the last operating sugar-beet processing plant in Colorado. For a buyer that means steady year-round rental demand and a housing stock with real range — brick and frame homes in the older grid near downtown, mid-century neighborhoods, newer subdivisions on the edges, and farm and ranch acreage outside the city limits where well and septic replace municipal utilities.

frederick.meta: Welcome to Frederick. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
frederick.welcome: Frederick, Colorado, is a dynamic and growing town that combines small-town charm with modern living. Located in Weld County, it offers a welcoming community, scenic parks, and a rich history rooted in its mining heritage. With its convenient location near Denver and Boulder, Frederick provides easy access to big-city amenities while maintaining a peaceful, family-friendly atmosphere.
frederick.things_to_do: Explore Frederick's Art in Public Places program, featuring public art installations and murals throughout town. Visit the Frederick Recreation Area, a 129-acre park offering a playground, picnic areas, a fishing pond, and paved walking trails around Milavec Reservoir. Learn about Frederick's mining heritage at the Miners Memorial Museum in Crist Park, open on a limited schedule (by request and select town events). Golf enthusiasts can tee off at the Bella Rosa Golf Course, a nine-hole course for players of all skill levels.
frederick.restaurants: Mirror Image Brewing Company is a local brewery and brewpub, Rumbo 52 Cocina & Cantina covers Mexican fare, and Georgia Boys BBQ Smokehouse serves up barbecue.
frederick.dog_parks: Frederick has its own dog park on-site at the Frederick Recreation Area.
frederick.hikes: The Frederick Recreation Area has 1.26 miles of crusher-fine trail around Milavec Reservoir plus 1.7 miles of paved trail, right in town. The St. Vrain Greenway Trail through nearby Longmont adds a longer paved option.
frederick.school_district: St. Vrain Valley Schools (feeds into Frederick High School)
frederick.commute: About 28 miles / 28-37 minutes to Denver and roughly 22 miles / 34 minutes to Boulder — a fairly balanced commute to both metro job centers.
frederick.relocate_extra: Frederick is one of the fastest-growing towns in the region, up roughly 30% since the 2020 census, fueled by Denver/Boulder-area buyers seeking affordability.

greeley.meta: Welcome to Greeley. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
greeley.welcome: Greeley, Colorado, is a vibrant city with a rich history and a thriving cultural scene. As a hub of Northern Colorado, it combines urban amenities with a welcoming, small-town feel. Known for its strong agricultural roots, excellent schools, and diverse recreational opportunities, Greeley offers a dynamic lifestyle surrounded by the natural beauty of the region.
greeley.things_to_do: Explore an extensive collection of model trains and intricate layouts at the Colorado Model Railroad Museum. Enjoy a scenic walk or bike ride along the Poudre River Trail, a 21-mile paved path with access to the Cache la Poudre River for fishing and wildlife observation. Step back in time at the Centennial Village Museum, an 8-acre living history experience showcasing over 35 unique structures, costumed interpreters, and heritage farm animals. Attend a performance at the Union Colony Civic Center, one of Northern Colorado's premier performing arts venues, hosting Broadway musicals, concerts, and local productions. Experience the annual Greeley Independence Stampede, a PRCA-sanctioned rodeo and summer festival featuring concerts, a demolition derby, and a Fourth of July parade.
greeley.restaurants: Greeley's dining scene mixes destination craft beer with longtime local favorites. WeldWerks Brewing Co. is an award-winning brewery known well beyond Weld County for its burgers and rotating small-batch beers. For a sit-down Italian dinner, locals point to Pellegrini Cucina Italiana, while Roasty's Diner, a downtown Greeley institution since the early 1970s (under new ownership since 2022, still serving its old-school breakfast and lunch menu plus a new Greek bakery case), is a local go-to.
greeley.dog_parks: Greeley has two dedicated off-leash dog parks: Island Grove Dog Park (14th Ave & D St), with separate small- and large-dog areas, and Rover Run Dog Park (near 5th Ave, adjacent to the Poudre River Trail), a fenced 3-acre area with a covered shelter.
greeley.hikes: The Poudre River Trail itself is Greeley's most walked/biked route, running 21 paved miles along the Cache la Poudre River. For a short in-town nature loop, Glenmere Park's roughly 0.8-mile paved trail circles a lake with abundant birdlife. For a true hike, many locals make the drive northeast to the Pawnee Buttes Trail in Pawnee National Grassland.
greeley.commute: About 32 miles / 45-50 minutes to Fort Collins via US-34; about 57-63 miles / roughly 1 hour to Denver via I-25 or US-85.
greeley.relocate_extra: Weld County was Colorado's fastest-growing large county in 2025, surpassing Larimer County in total population for the first time.

johnstown.meta: Welcome to Johnstown. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
johnstown.welcome: Johnstown, Colorado, is a charming and rapidly growing town that perfectly blends small-town warmth with modern conveniences. Located near Loveland and Greeley, it offers a friendly community atmosphere, excellent schools, and easy access to Northern Colorado’s amenities. With its scenic landscapes and family-oriented vibe, Johnstown is an inviting place to call home.
johnstown.things_to_do: Experience live theater performances paired with dining at the Candlelight Dinner Playhouse, known for its engaging shows and quality service. Enjoy outdoor activities at Parish Park, which features open green spaces, playgrounds, and facilities suitable for family gatherings and recreational pursuits. Learn about Johnstown's history at the Historic Parish House and Museum, an Arts and Crafts-style home of the town's founder, showcasing local artifacts and exhibits. For shooting enthusiasts, the Liberty Firearms Institute offers a state-of-the-art shooting range, training courses, and a retail store with a wide selection of firearms and accessories. Participate in various fitness and community programs at the Johnstown Community YMCA, which offers facilities like swimming pools, gyms, and group classes for all ages.
johnstown.restaurants: Right off I-25 sits the regionally famous Johnson's Corner truck stop, long known for its cinnamon rolls. For breakfast in town, Urban Egg and Daytime Eatery serves organic, made-from-scratch fare, and Bonefish Grill at the Johnstown/Centerra line covers seafood.
johnstown.dog_parks: There is no confirmed dedicated off-leash dog park inside Johnstown town limits — Parish Park and other town parks require dogs on-leash. The nearest off-leash options are in neighboring Loveland (Fairgrounds Park dog park) or Timnath (WildWing Park), roughly 10-15 minutes away.
johnstown.hikes: Johnstown itself is light on formal trailheads, but Parish Park has paved walking paths for an easy stroll. For real hiking, most residents drive 15-20 minutes to the Poudre River Trail or to Devil's Backbone Open Space in Loveland.
johnstown.commute: About 12 miles / 21 minutes to Loveland via CO-402; about 47 miles / under an hour to Denver via I-25.
johnstown.relocate_extra: The adjacent Centerra South development has been rebranded Avenue South, with new construction underway as of 2026, adding to Johnstown-area retail and residential growth.

lafayette.meta: Welcome to Lafayette. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
lafayette.welcome: Lafayette, Colorado, is a charming and vibrant city that perfectly blends small-town warmth with modern amenities. Located in Boulder County, it offers a thriving arts scene, beautiful parks, and a welcoming community. With its stunning views of the Rocky Mountains and a focus on sustainability and local culture, Lafayette is an inviting place to call home.
lafayette.things_to_do: Enjoy outdoor activities at Waneka Lake Park, a 147-acre recreational area featuring a 1.2-mile fitness trail, playgrounds, and opportunities for fishing and boating on the lake. Explore local history at the Lafayette Miners Museum, which showcases artifacts related to the city's coal mining heritage. Discover Lafayette's creative side with public art and murals throughout Old Town. Visit The Collective, Lafayette's community arts center, which hosts rotating art exhibits and workshops. Participate in Lafayette's annual Peach Festival each August, celebrating the region's peach harvest with food, music, and crafts.
lafayette.restaurants: Acreage by Stem Ciders offers high-elevation dining with mountain views alongside house-made ciders. Teocalli Cocina is a local favorite for authentic Mexican fare, and The Post Chicken & Beer is famous regionwide for its gluten-free fried chicken paired with local craft beer.
lafayette.dog_parks: Dog owners in Lafayette head to The Great Bark Dog Park, a fenced 6.1-acre off-leash area at 597 N. 119th St. with a separate small-dog section, open daily 6am-10pm.
lafayette.hikes: The Waneka Lake Trail, the 1.2-mile loop around Waneka Lake, is an easy, scenic walk right in town with wildlife viewing at the adjoining Greenlee Wildlife Preserve. The Coal Creek Trail is a flat, paved multi-use path connecting Lafayette to neighboring Louisville and Superior.
lafayette.commute: About 30 miles / roughly 43 minutes to Loveland via US-287/CO-7.
lafayette.relocate_extra: Lafayette is often positioned as the relative value play inside Boulder Valley School District — same district access as Boulder and Louisville, typically at a lower price point.

log-lane-village.meta: Welcome to Log Lane Village. Explore Morgan County's smallest incorporated town — about 900 people at the I-76 and Highway 144 crossroads, two miles from everything Fort Morgan has.
log-lane-village.welcome: Log Lane Village is a statutory town of about 900 people (913 at the 2020 census), incorporated in 1956 and named for the log houses it started as, at the crossroads of Highway 144 and I-76 about two miles northwest of Fort Morgan. It is residential almost end to end — a grid of small lots, a town hall on Birch Street, a Dollar General, a convenience and liquor store, a couple of auto shops, a light-industrial fabrication shop, and, unusually for a town this size, four licensed marijuana dispensaries, which the town's own economic development page lists first among its businesses. What buyers get here is a quiet lot two miles from everything Fort Morgan has: a hospital, a community college campus, and a river park.
log-lane-village.things_to_do: The town runs a real calendar for its size — an Easter egg hunt, Independence Day fireworks, a summer town barbecue and National Night Out, a car show and fall festival, trunk-or-treat at Halloween, and a kids' Christmas party. Past that, everything is Fort Morgan, two miles southeast: Riverside Park's trails, ponds and summer pool, the Fort Morgan Museum on Main Street, and the pedestrian Rainbow Arch Bridge over the South Platte.
log-lane-village.restaurants: There are no sit-down restaurants in Log Lane Village — the business base is a Dollar General, a convenience and liquor store, and auto and fabrication shops. Dining means the two-mile drive into Fort Morgan, where Main Street has Cables Pub and Grill, Bun Appetit and Kukaro Brewing, or 13 miles east to True Grits Steakhouse in Brush.
log-lane-village.dog_parks: No dog park in town. Fort Morgan's two fenced off-leash parks — the split large- and small-dog park at Gateway Park and the smaller one at Fulton Heights Park — are both a few minutes away, and Riverside Park's river trails are the everyday leashed walk.
log-lane-village.hikes: Nothing in town, and nothing pretending otherwise. The closest real walking is Riverside Park's roughly six miles of South Platte trails in Fort Morgan, two miles away. Jackson Lake State Park is about a half-hour west, and the nearest mountain trailheads are a two-hour drive.
log-lane-village.school_district: Morgan County School District Re-3 (Fort Morgan)
log-lane-village.commute: Two miles to Fort Morgan, about 83 miles and an hour and a half to Denver on I-76, and about 55 miles to Greeley — functionally the same commute as Fort Morgan's, with the interstate on-ramp right there at the Highway 144 interchange.
log-lane-village.relocate_extra: Log Lane Village is worth understanding before buying into it. It's its own municipality rather than part of Fort Morgan, with its own town hall, ordinances and utility service, so water, sewer and trash come from the town — ask what the monthly utility bill actually runs, and whether the specific lot is on town water and sewer, because this is an older small-lot town and that detail varies house to house. Children attend Morgan County School District Re-3 schools in Fort Morgan. And know the local character going in: four retail marijuana dispensaries in a town of 900 is a defining feature of the place, and the town lists them among its primary businesses.

longmont.meta: Welcome to Longmont. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
longmont.welcome: Longmont is the practical answer to Boulder. It is a city of roughly 97,000 sixteen miles up the road, with its own real downtown rather than a commercial strip, and it is where a great many people end up when they love Boulder County and want to own something larger than a condo. It is also one of the few Front Range cities that genuinely spans two counties — most of Longmont sits in Boulder County, part of it in Weld — which affects taxes, services and which county offices you deal with, and is worth establishing about a specific address rather than assuming.
longmont.things_to_do: Downtown Longmont's Main Street is a working main street rather than a restored one, active since the late 1800s and lined with restaurants, boutiques and galleries. Union Reservoir, four miles east of downtown, is a 736-acre city-owned reservoir and nature area open daily for a small entry fee — swimming, paddling, fishing and shoreline walking, and one of the few places on the northern Front Range where you can do all of that inside city limits. St. Vrain State Park sits just outside town.
longmont.restaurants: The food is concentrated on and around Main Street downtown, walkable across a handful of blocks, which is unusual for a Front Range city this size — most have their dining spread along an arterial road instead. It ranges from long-standing family restaurants to newer kitchens and taprooms, and the district is busy on weeknights rather than only at weekends.
longmont.dog_parks: The city runs off-leash areas and the St. Vrain Greenway gives a long, mostly flat paved corridor through town that most local dog owners use daily. Union Reservoir allows leashed dogs in its day-use areas. Worth knowing if you are moving from further west: unlike the mountain open spaces above Lyons and Boulder, Longmont's trail system is dog-friendly throughout.
longmont.hikes: Longmont's own walking is the St. Vrain Greenway, a paved corridor following the creek through the city, plus the shoreline trail at Union Reservoir. For real elevation, the Boulder County open spaces at Hall Ranch and Heil Valley Ranch are a short drive northwest toward Lyons, and Rocky Mountain National Park is reachable up US-36 through Lyons and Estes Park.
longmont.commute: About 16 miles to Boulder, and roughly 33 miles / about 43 minutes to Denver. St. Vrain Valley Schools, which serves the city, is Colorado's seventh largest district — around 33,000 students across 60 schools and 411 square miles — so school choice here is a genuine consideration rather than a formality.
longmont.relocate_extra: Longmont is where a lot of Boulder County buying decisions actually land. Sixteen miles buys materially more house than the same money does in Boulder, the downtown is real, and the commute is short enough that people do it for years. Two things to establish about any specific address: which county it sits in, since Longmont straddles the Boulder/Weld line, and how close it is to the St. Vrain corridor — the 2013 flood reached parts of Longmont too, and floodplain designation affects insurance and resale here just as it does upstream in Lyons.

louisville.meta: Welcome to Louisville. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
louisville.welcome: Louisville, Colorado, is a picturesque city celebrated for its friendly community, scenic beauty, and high quality of life. Nestled in Boulder County, it offers charming neighborhoods, vibrant local shops, and an abundance of parks and trails. With its small-town charm and easy access to Denver and Boulder, Louisville is a delightful place to live, work, and play.
louisville.things_to_do: Stroll through Historic Downtown Louisville, where you'll find charming streets lined with unique shops, restaurants, and art galleries. Experience local flavors at the Louisville Farmers Market, held Saturdays from May to October along Front Street. Enjoy panoramic views of the Flatirons and the Front Range from Davidson Mesa, a roughly 3.2-mile loop trail that's perfect for walking, biking, and wildlife observation. Delve into the city's rich past at the Louisville Historical Museum, which features exhibits on local history, including the area's coal mining heritage.
louisville.restaurants: Huckleberry is the local go-to for breakfast/brunch, especially its stuffed French toast. Karen's Country Kitchen and Italian favorite Parma Trattoria and Mozzarella Bar draw regular crowds, while Sweet Cow is the beloved local ice cream stop that's practically a Louisville tradition.
louisville.dog_parks: Louisville maintains two official off-leash areas: the fenced Community Park Dog Park at 955 Bella Vista Drive, and the Davidson Mesa Open Space Off-Leash Area near McCaslin Blvd — easy to combine a hike and off-leash time in the same spot.
louisville.hikes: Davidson Mesa is the hometown favorite: a rolling, easy loop (roughly 3.2 miles) with sweeping views of the Front Range and Flatirons. The Coal Creek Trail runs through Louisville as a flat, paved path connecting to Lafayette and Superior.
louisville.commute: About 32 miles / roughly 48 minutes to Loveland via US-287.
louisville.relocate_extra: Louisville has a well-documented history of national "Best Places to Live" recognition, a reputation that continues to support strong buyer demand and price premiums relative to nearby towns.

loveland.meta: Welcome to Loveland. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
loveland.welcome: Loveland, Colorado, is a charming city celebrated for its artistic vibe, scenic beauty, and warm community spirit. Nestled near the Rocky Mountains, it offers stunning landscapes, a rich arts scene, and plenty of opportunities for outdoor adventures. Known as the “Sweetheart City,” Loveland blends creativity and nature seamlessly, making it a unique and inviting place to live.
loveland.things_to_do: Explore the Benson Park Sculpture Garden, featuring over 150 unique sculptures set amidst beautifully landscaped grounds. It's a perfect spot for art enthusiasts and families alike. Devil's Backbone Open Space Hike the Devil's Backbone Nature Trail, known for its distinctive rock formations and panoramic views. This area offers trails suitable for various skill levels. Enjoy a day of boating, fishing, or swimming at Boyd Lake State Park. The park also provides picnic areas and trails for biking and hiking. Delve into local history and art at the Loveland Museum, which offers a range of exhibits, educational programs, and events throughout the year. Visit the Chapungu Sculpture Park, a 26-acre park showcasing stone sculptures from Zimbabwean artists, complemented by walking paths and water features. Catch a live performance or film at the historic Rialto Theater Center, a beautifully restored venue that hosts a variety of cultural events.
loveland.restaurants: Loveland's dining scene ranges from award-winning barbecue to craft beer. Nordy's Bar-B-Que & Grill is a longtime local favorite for smoked meats, while Door 222 Food & Drink covers upscale steak-and-seafood nights out. For casual sips, Verboten Brewing and Loveland Aleworks are both well-loved, independently owned local breweries with regularly rotating taps.
loveland.dog_parks: Loveland's main off-leash area is the Dog Park at Fairgrounds Park (700 S. Railroad Ave), a city-run facility with separate fenced sections for large and small dogs and a water fountain. Many of the city's natural areas, including trails along the Big Thompson River, are leashed-dog-friendly as well.
loveland.hikes: Devil's Backbone Open Space remains the signature hike, with roughly 12 miles of trail leading to the landmark rock formation known as the Keyhole. For an easier outing, the Round Mountain Foothills Nature Trail is a gentle one-mile loop, and Prairie Ridge Natural Area offers a 2.4-mile multi-use trail system in northwest Loveland.
loveland.commute: About 51 miles / roughly 1 hour 4 minutes to Denver via I-25; about 33 miles / roughly 49 minutes to Boulder via CO-119.
loveland.relocate_extra: Loveland hosts Sculpture in the Park each August at Benson Park, one of the largest outdoor fine-art sculpture shows in the country — a signature annual event tied to the city's arts-town identity.

lyons.meta: Welcome to Lyons. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
lyons.welcome: Lyons sits where the North and South St. Vrain Creeks meet, at the point where the plains stop and the foothills start — which is why it has been called the double gateway to the Rockies. It is a small town with an outsized cultural footprint: Planet Bluegrass has run its twenty-acre festival ranch here since 1994, and Oskar Blues started in Lyons in 1997. What buyers notice first is that it does not feel like a Boulder County commuter suburb. It feels like a mountain town that happens to be twenty minutes from Longmont.
lyons.things_to_do: Planet Bluegrass's ranch on the edge of town hosts RockyGrass and the Rocky Mountain Folks Festival, which reshape the town for a weekend at a time and are a genuine reason people move here. Main Street is walkable and small — a handful of restaurants, galleries and shops rather than a strip. La Mariposa Restaurant & Margarita House at 112 E Main St is a local fixture, cooking from scratch across all eight regions of Mexico with a list of more than forty margaritas. From town, CO-7 climbs toward Estes Park and Rocky Mountain National Park, and the Peak to Peak Highway is right there.
lyons.restaurants: Dining is concentrated on and just off Main Street, walkable end to end. La Mariposa Restaurant & Margarita House is the long-standing Mexican kitchen in the middle of it — scratch cooking, generous portions, and a margarita list people drive up for. Lyons also has the distinction of being where Oskar Blues began in 1997, which tells you something about how seriously a town of this size takes its beer.
lyons.dog_parks: Worth knowing before you move here with a dog: Heil Valley Ranch, the 5,000-acre open space between Lyons and Boulder, does not allow dogs at all, for wildlife reasons. That surprises people who buy here specifically for the trail access. The St. Vrain corridor through town and the trails at Hall Ranch are where most local dog owners actually go, and leash rules apply on Boulder County Open Space.
lyons.hikes: Lyons sits between two large pieces of Boulder County Open Space. Hall Ranch is the closer of the two, right at the edge of town, and Heil Valley Ranch covers about 5,000 acres of ponderosa and open hillside between Lyons and Boulder — both part of the North Foothills Open Space, and connected to each other by the Picture Rock Trail, which means you can genuinely ride or walk between them. Trailheads are reachable from town itself, which is unusual and is a large part of why people pay to live here.
lyons.school_district: St. Vrain Valley Schools (Lyons Elementary and Lyons Middle/Senior High)
lyons.commute: About 12 miles / roughly 20 minutes to Longmont via US-36 and CO-66, and about 17 miles / roughly 30 minutes to Boulder — close enough that Lyons works as a real commuter base, far enough that it does not feel like one. Estes Park and Rocky Mountain National Park are up CO-7 from town.
lyons.relocate_extra: One thing to understand about Lyons before making an offer. The September 2013 flood sent both branches of the St. Vrain through the middle of town, destroying homes, businesses and the festival grounds and displacing thousands of people. The town rebuilt and is thriving — but floodplain designation, flood insurance requirements and what was rebuilt when are real questions on any property near the creeks, and they materially affect cost and resale. Ask them before you write an offer, not after inspection. Christine works throughout Boulder County and will tell you plainly which properties carry that question and which do not.

masonville.meta: Welcome to Masonville. Explore this unincorporated Larimer County community near Horsetooth Reservoir and the foothills west of Fort Collins and Loveland.
masonville.welcome: Masonville is a small unincorporated community tucked into the foothills of western Larimer County, between Fort Collins and Loveland near Horsetooth Reservoir and Masonville Falls. It draws buyers looking for acreage, privacy, and mountain views without giving up easy access to town — historic ranch land, custom foothill homes, and some of the quietest country roads in the county.
masonville.things_to_do: Masonville sits right at the edge of Larimer County open space, with Horsetooth Reservoir and Horsetooth Mountain Open Space just minutes away — 29 miles of trails, boating, rock climbing, and the seasonal Horsetooth Falls (best seen during spring runoff). The historic Masonville Mercantile — now in its 130th season under new ownership after a 2024 sale — built in 1896 by town founder James Mason and reopened under new ownership in 2025, anchors the tiny community center. Redstone Canyon Road offers a scenic drive through the area, though most of the surrounding canyon is private ranch land.
masonville.restaurants: Masonville itself has essentially no commercial dining — it's a tiny unincorporated crossroads community. The closest real options are back toward Loveland (Nordy's Bar-B-Que & Grill, Door 222 Food & Drink) or the restaurants of Old Town Fort Collins, both a short drive away.
masonville.dog_parks: There is no dedicated off-leash dog park in Masonville itself. The nearest options are Spring Canyon Dog Park in Fort Collins and the Dog Park at Fairgrounds Park in Loveland, both roughly a 15-20 minute drive. Dogs must stay leashed on Horsetooth Mountain Open Space's own trails.
masonville.hikes: Horsetooth Mountain Open Space is the star attraction, with 29 miles of trails including the climb to Horsetooth Rock and the seasonal Horsetooth Falls. The open space connects directly to the Blue Sky Trail and Lory State Park's trail system for longer point-to-point hikes.
masonville.commute: About 15 miles (30 min) to Fort Collins and about 12 miles (25 min) to Loveland via county roads — both easy day-trip commutes for an unincorporated foothills community.
masonville.relocate_extra: Real estate in Masonville skews toward large rural acreage rather than typical subdivision lots — the Redstone Canyon neighborhood, for example, originated from ranches subdivided into 40-acre parcels in the late 1960s — so buyers should expect well-and-septic, larger-lot living rather than municipal utilities.

mead.meta: Welcome to Mead. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
mead.welcome: Mead, Colorado, is a tranquil and friendly town that captures the essence of small-town living. Nestled between Longmont and Loveland, it offers beautiful open spaces, a strong sense of community, and easy access to Northern Colorado’s amenities. With its peaceful neighborhoods and scenic charm, Mead is a wonderful place to call home.
mead.things_to_do: Visit the historic Highlandlake Church, built in 1896 and placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1989, which still stands and offers a glimpse into the area's past. Located about 7 miles south of Mead, St. Vrain State Park offers roughly 689 acres of land and 228 acres of water, making it a perfect place for camping, birdwatching, fishing, and hiking. The town of Mead also offers several public parks and walking trails for outdoor recreation and community gatherings.
mead.restaurants: Josie's Tacos on Main Street is a favorite for quick, authentic Mexican food, while Ranchero's Restaurant and Mead Pizza Plus, both on Hwy 66, serve up comfort food for locals. Coffee lovers should note Mead is home to the headquarters of Ziggi's Coffee, the regional drive-thru coffee chain.
mead.dog_parks: Mead doesn't have its own dedicated off-leash dog park. The nearest real options are in Longmont, about 10-15 minutes away, including Rough and Ready Neighborhood Park and Blue Skies Neighborhood Park, both with fenced off-leash dog runs.
mead.hikes: St. Vrain State Park, just south of town, has easy, flat walking trails around its ponds, ideal for casual walks and birdwatching. In town, the walking loop at Lorin Mead Park at Highland Lake offers a quieter, close-to-home option.
mead.school_district: St. Vrain Valley School District RE-1J
mead.commute: About 13 miles / 18 minutes to Longmont via I-25; about 17 miles / 24 minutes to Loveland via I-25.

milliken.meta: Welcome to Milliken. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
milliken.welcome: Milliken, Colorado, is a peaceful and welcoming town known for its close-knit community and small-town charm. Situated along the South Platte River, it offers scenic beauty, a relaxed pace of life, and easy access to nearby cities like Greeley and Loveland. With its friendly atmosphere and emphasis on outdoor living, Milliken is an ideal place to enjoy Colorado’s natural beauty and community spirit.
milliken.things_to_do: Built in 1911, the Daniels School is the last standing rural brick schoolhouse in Weld County and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. It operated for nearly 50 years (1911-1959) and now serves as a historical landmark. Ehrlich Lake and Centennial Lake provide short walking trails and are stocked with fish by Colorado Parks & Wildlife, making them perfect spots for fishing and leisurely strolls. For golf enthusiasts, The Mad Russian Golf Club offers a scenic 18-hole course. Skateboarders can visit the Milliken Skatepark.
milliken.restaurants: Mill Haüs Coffee is a local coffee shop and bakery serving paninis and pastries — a real neighborhood gathering spot. For a casual meal, El Mex-Kal Restaurant offers dine-in and takeout Mexican food.
milliken.dog_parks: Milliken has its own dedicated off-leash area: the Milliken Dog Park, the only spot in town where dogs are permitted off-leash — leashes are required everywhere else in town parks.
milliken.hikes: Ehrlich Lake and Centennial Lake both have short, easy walking trails looping the water. The South Platte River, which runs along town, also offers informal walking and fishing access.
milliken.commute: About 14 miles / 27 minutes to Greeley via US-34 Business; about 15 miles / 27 minutes to Loveland via CO-60.
milliken.relocate_extra: Milliken sits within Weld County's high-growth corridor — the county was Colorado's fastest-growing large county in 2025, adding nearly 50,000 residents since 2020.

nederland.meta: Welcome to Nederland. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
nederland.welcome: Nederland, Colorado, is a quaint mountain town known for its rich history, artistic spirit, and stunning natural surroundings. Located in Boulder County near the Continental Divide, it offers a peaceful, laid-back lifestyle with access to endless outdoor adventures. With its unique charm and strong sense of community, Nederland is a perfect retreat for those seeking a connection to nature and a welcoming mountain vibe.
nederland.things_to_do: Experience the Carousel of Happiness, a hand-carved, restored 1910 Looff carousel featuring 56 whimsical animals, accompanied by the music of a 1913 Wurlitzer band organ. Eldora Mountain Resort offers skiing and snowboarding in winter, with the surrounding Indian Peaks Wilderness open for summer hiking. Explore the outdoors via the Hessie Trailhead, a gateway to numerous hiking trails leading to alpine lakes. Delve into the town's rich mining history at the Nederland Mining Museum, open seasonally June through October. Relax by Barker Reservoir, a scenic spot ideal for picnics, fishing, and mountain views.
nederland.restaurants: Crosscut Pizzeria & Taphouse is well-loved for wood-fired pizza and a mountain-town patio. Kathmandu Restaurant brings genuine Nepali and Indian cuisine to a town better known for burgers than curry, and Salto Coffee Works is the local go-to for espresso before a day on the trails.
nederland.dog_parks: Nederland itself does not have a dedicated fenced dog park. Dogs are welcome off-leash under voice-and-sight control on many surrounding Boulder County and U.S. Forest Service trails near town. For a true fenced off-leash dog park, the nearest options are down the canyon in Boulder, about 17 miles (roughly a 30-35 minute drive).
nederland.hikes: From the Hessie Trailhead, the hike to Lost Lake is a short, scenic favorite with wildflowers and mountain views. Diamond Lake and Devil's Thumb Lake are popular longer hikes into the Indian Peaks Wilderness, and the trail around Barker Reservoir offers an easy, flat walk right at Nederland's edge.
nederland.school_district: Boulder Valley School District (BVSD, Re-2) — served locally by Nederland Elementary and Nederland Middle-Senior High School
nederland.commute: About 49 miles / roughly 1 hour 20 minutes to Loveland via CO-119/US-36; about 17 miles / roughly 32 minutes to Boulder.
nederland.relocate_extra: Nederland's town board approved a roughly $120M purchase of Eldora Mountain Resort from POWDR Corporation (approved January 2026) — if finalized, Eldora would become a rare community/municipally-owned ski resort, a distinctive story for buyers drawn to mountain-town character.

nunn.meta: Welcome to Nunn. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
nunn.welcome: Nunn is a town of about 550 people on US-85 north of Greeley, and it is one of the few places on the northern Front Range where acreage is still genuinely attainable. Almost nobody buys in Nunn for the town itself — they buy for the land: twenty, thirty-five, forty-five acres, no HOA, and horizon in every direction. That makes it a completely different purchase from a house in a subdivision, and the difference is where people get hurt.
nunn.things_to_do: Nunn is small and unpretentious — a handful of local businesses along US-85 and the highway itself, which is the main street. What people come here for is outside: wide-open shortgrass prairie, uninterrupted views west to the Front Range, and enough sky that you can watch weather arrive an hour before it does. The one destination that draws people from all over the Front Range is Great Guns Sporting at 16126 County Road 96 — a public outdoor range open seven days a week with 42 rifle positions from 25 to 300 yards, 36 pistol positions, three action bays, a 15-station sporting clays course, five trap fields, two skeet fields and a five-stand. It has been open to the public since 1996 and is a real reason some buyers choose this side of Weld County. Greeley is twenty-one miles south for anything the town does not have, and Fort Collins is twenty-five miles southwest.
nunn.restaurants: Being straight about it: Nunn has no restaurant. The old cafe on 5th Street — Nunn Cafe, latterly Tumble Weed — is closed, and directory sites still listing it as open are wrong. Soaring V Fuels on County Road 100 is the fuel and convenience stop in town, and that is the extent of it. Nunn residents shop and eat in Ault, twelve miles south, or in Greeley. The nearest-restaurant panel above reads live from Google so it stays honest as places open and close. If a twelve-mile drive for dinner sounds like a drawback, Nunn is probably not your town; if it sounds like the point, it probably is.
nunn.dog_parks: There is no municipal dog park, and for most people who buy here that is irrelevant — the property is the dog park. What matters instead is fencing, and whether existing fence lines actually follow the survey. On acreage this is worth confirming rather than assuming, because moving a fence is expensive and neighbourly disagreements about where one belongs are common out here.
nunn.hikes: This is not trail country in the sense that Lyons or Estes Park is — it is open prairie, and most of the land around Nunn is private or state trust land rather than public open space. Pawnee National Grassland lies east of town, with the Pawnee Buttes trail its best-known walk. For mountain trails, people here drive to the foothills west of Fort Collins.
nunn.school_district: Weld RE-9 School District (Highland — serving Ault, Pierce, Nunn and Carr)
nunn.commute: About 21 miles to Greeley via US-85 and CR 29, and about 25 miles to Fort Collins. Both are real commutes rather than errands, and the school district — Weld RE-9, known locally as Highland — runs bus routes across 539 square miles, which tells you something honest about the distances out here.
nunn.relocate_extra: If you are buying land in Nunn, this is the part that matters more than the house.
