A property here is not a subdivision lot: there are wells and well permits, septic systems and their condition, water rights, survey lines, easements and legal access, utility distances, county zoning, and rules on how many animals you may keep and where. Every one of those can change what a parcel is worth or whether you can do the thing you bought it for. If shooting is part of why you are looking out here, note that Great Guns Sporting sits on County Road 96, which is a genuine amenity to some buyers and something to know about in advance for others — it is an outdoor range, and sound carries a long way across open prairie. Many Nunn properties are also USDA-eligible, which can mean no down payment — genuinely useful, and it comes with its own conditions. Christine has listed and sold acreage in and around Nunn repeatedly and will walk the property with you asking these questions before you write an offer, not after.

red-feather-lakes.meta: Welcome to Red Feather Lakes. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
red-feather-lakes.welcome: Red Feather Lakes, Colorado, is a serene mountain village offering a peaceful retreat surrounded by breathtaking natural beauty. Tucked away in the Roosevelt National Forest, it’s a haven for outdoor enthusiasts with endless opportunities for hiking, fishing, and wildlife watching. Known for its tranquil lakes and rustic charm, Red Feather Lakes is the perfect escape for those seeking a quiet, nature-focused lifestyle.
red-feather-lakes.things_to_do: Formerly known as Shambhala Mountain Center, the Drala Mountain Center is a renowned Buddhist retreat home to the Great Stupa of Dharmakaya, widely described as the largest stupa in North America. Enjoy outdoor activities at Dowdy Lake, a 115-acre reservoir ideal for kayaking, canoeing, and fishing, with a 2.3-mile trail looping the water. Experience the whimsical charm of Gnome Road, a dirt path lined with ceramic gnomes and fairy doors. For panoramic views, visit Deadman Lookout, a historic fire tower. Golf enthusiasts can play a round at The Golf Club at Fox Acres, an 18-hole course open to the public since 2014.
red-feather-lakes.restaurants: Dining options are intentionally low-key given the setting. The Tavern at Red Feather Lakes is the classic local spot for a burger and a cold beer, and Potbelly Restaurant is known for homemade pies and hearty comfort food. A bit further out toward Livermore, the historic Forks Mercantity and Saloon is a well-known roadside landmark for a meal on the way in or out.
red-feather-lakes.dog_parks: Red Feather Lakes itself has no formal dog park — it's rural mountain terrain where dogs typically go leashed or under voice control on trails and forest roads within the surrounding Roosevelt National Forest. For a true fenced off-leash dog park, the nearest option is in Fort Collins, about 45 miles (roughly 70 minutes) away.
red-feather-lakes.hikes: The Dowdy Lake Trail (2.3-mile loop) circles the largest lake in the Red Feather Lakes chain. The Lady Moon and Molly Moon Trail (roughly 6.5 miles round trip) is a favorite for a longer forest hike with moderate elevation gain.
red-feather-lakes.school_district: Poudre School District R-1 (local schooling via PSD's Mountain Schools cluster, including Red Feather Lakes Elementary; older students bus toward Fort Collins/Laporte schools)
red-feather-lakes.commute: About 45 miles / roughly 1 hour 10 minutes to Fort Collins via CR 74E — the primary commute route and nearest job center.
red-feather-lakes.relocate_extra: Real estate here is dominated by well-and-septic, large-acreage mountain and cabin lots (often 1+ acres, many seasonal or off-grid) — a distinctly different buyer profile than the platted town lots common down on the plains.

severance.meta: Welcome to Severance. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
severance.welcome: Severance, Colorado, is a charming and rapidly growing town nestled in Northern Colorado. Known for its friendly community and scenic surroundings, Severance offers a perfect blend of small-town charm and modern development. With open spaces, great schools, and a relaxed pace of life, it’s an inviting place to settle and enjoy the beauty of Colorado living.
severance.things_to_do: A local landmark first opened in 1957 (closed briefly in the mid-2000s and reopened under new ownership in 2008, carrying forward the original building and recipes), Bruce's Bar is renowned for its Rocky Mountain oysters and live music. Explore firefighting history at the Windsor-Severance Fire Museum (located just south in Windsor), which houses antique fire trucks and memorabilia. Located about six miles south in Windsor, Windsor Lake features a scenic 2.25-mile trail around its perimeter, a swim beach, and opportunities for fishing and boating. Outdoor enthusiasts can enjoy the Great Western Trail, a 10.5-mile mixed-use path through Weld County. Note: Severance's Community Park closed in early 2026 for a construction/improvement phase expected to run through fall 2026, so Severance Days and the town's usual summer concert series have shifted to alternate venues and a later date for the year.
severance.restaurants: Bruce's Bar, a genuine Colorado landmark first opened in 1957 and reopened under new ownership in 2008, remains the town's marquee stop for Rocky Mountain oysters, buffalo and elk burgers, and live music. For casual Mexican food, Tecate Grill Severance is a local option, and Shebrews Coffee and Ice Cream rounds things out for a sweet treat.
severance.dog_parks: Severance doesn't have its own dog park, but just down the road in Windsor, the Windsor Lake Trail & Dog Park offers a fenced off-leash area with direct lake access.
severance.hikes: The Great Western Trail (10.5 miles, mixed-use, running through Windsor, Severance, and Eaton on a former rail bed) is the area's standout trail. The Windsor Lake Trail, a 2.25-mile paved path circling the lake in nearby Windsor, is an easy, scenic walking loop with its own dog park built in.
severance.commute: About 16 miles / 27 minutes to Fort Collins via CO-14.
severance.relocate_extra: Severance is one of Weld County's fastest-growing communities, reflecting continued new-home construction in and around town.

timnath.meta: Welcome to Timnath. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
timnath.welcome: Timnath, Colorado, is a peaceful and rapidly growing town that perfectly balances small-town charm with modern living. Located just east of Fort Collins, it offers beautiful open spaces, family-friendly neighborhoods, and a strong sense of community. With its stunning views of the Rockies and easy access to outdoor activities, Timnath is an idyllic place to call home.
timnath.things_to_do: Enjoy fishing, boating, and bird-watching at Timnath Reservoir, a popular spot for outdoor enthusiasts. Visit Timnath Beerwerks to sample a variety of craft beers, with regular food-truck visits and live music. Stroll through Historic Old Town Timnath, featuring historic buildings, local shops, and eateries. Nearby, the Arapaho Bend Natural Area — a City of Fort Collins natural area just west of Timnath — offers trails for hiking and wildlife viewing.
timnath.restaurants: The Farmhouse at Jessup Farm offers farm-to-table dining in a restored historic farmhouse at Jessup Farm Artisan Village. Timnath Beerwerks pairs rotating craft beer with regular food-truck visits, and Doug's Diner is a longtime local breakfast-and-lunch spot.
timnath.dog_parks: Timnath has its own dedicated off-leash Timnath Dog Park, and the newer WildWing Park (opened 2025) also includes a designated dog park area — leashes are required elsewhere in town parks.
timnath.hikes: The paved Poudre River Trail runs directly through Timnath, connecting to Fort Collins and Greeley. Arapaho Bend Natural Area, just west near the Timnath/Fort Collins line, has an easy loop with ponds and prairie-dog colonies.
timnath.commute: About 10 miles (17 min) to Fort Collins via CO-14, and about 57 miles (roughly 1 hour 7 minutes) to Denver via I-25.
timnath.relocate_extra: Timnath's rapid growth is almost entirely master-planned-community development (WildWing, Timnath Ranch), and most of these communities layer both an HOA and a metropolitan district on top of base property taxes — a real budgeting factor for relocating buyers.

wellington.meta: Welcome to Wellington. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
wellington.welcome: Wellington, Colorado, is a quaint and welcoming town known for its friendly atmosphere and strong community ties. Located north of Fort Collins, it offers a relaxed pace of life with access to beautiful outdoor spaces and a growing local economy. With its small-town charm and proximity to the Rockies, Wellington is an ideal spot for those seeking a close-knit community and natural beauty.
wellington.things_to_do: Explore the Red Mountain Open Space, offering scenic trails for hiking, biking, and horseback riding amidst striking red rock formations. Visit the Old Colorado Brewing Company to enjoy handcrafted beers in a historic setting. Stroll through the seasonal Wellington Main Street Market, a recurring event featuring local vendors, fresh produce, and crafts. Relax at Viewpointe Park, a local green space offering playgrounds and open fields.
wellington.restaurants: Wellington Grill, locally owned by Jon & Donita Comes, is the town's classic American spot for burgers, steaks, and seafood, with a lively patio that hosts live music. Sol de Jalisco serves traditional Mexican fare, and T Bar Inn is a longtime local bar-and-grill.
wellington.dog_parks: Wellington has its own Wellington Dog Park (8760 Buffalo Creek Pkwy) — an off-leash facility with a self-serve dog wash station; note it requires a town membership and current vaccination records. For leashed walks, Red Mountain Open Space just north of town is popular with dog owners.
wellington.hikes: Red Mountain Open Space, including the Bent Rock Trail, offers striking red-rock formations right outside Wellington. Just north, Soapstone Prairie Natural Area has miles of rolling-prairie trails known for bison and wide-open views.
wellington.school_district: Poudre School District R-1 (Wellington Middle-High School serves the town)
wellington.commute: About 14 miles / roughly 20 minutes to Fort Collins via CO-1, Wellington's main commute corridor and primary job center.
wellington.relocate_extra: Wellington broke ground in 2025 on the 300-acre Sage Farms master-planned residential community, the Wellington Business Center retail/restaurant development, and a 50,000+ sq ft manufacturing facility — a shift from bedroom community toward more local jobs and amenities.

wiggins.meta: Welcome to Wiggins. Explore western Morgan County's fastest-growing small town — new-build homes at Kiowa Park, 15 miles from Fort Morgan and about an hour from Denver on I-76.
wiggins.welcome: Wiggins is the Morgan County town closest to Denver, and the one that has changed the most. It started as a railroad depot in 1882 and sat at roughly the same size for decades — then it started growing in earnest when Front Range buyers ran out of affordable options and began looking east along I-76. It's still small: about 1,200 people, one school campus, a short row of businesses on Central Avenue. But the Kiowa Park subdivision on the edge of town has added new construction that would look at home in a Denver suburb, and the town has been planning for a good deal more of it. Elevation 4,557 feet, wide-open sky, and the shortest Front Range commute in the county.
wiggins.things_to_do: Wiggins is a base camp more than a destination, and its best asset sits 13 miles north: Jackson Lake State Park, a warm-water reservoir with sandy beaches, 251 campsites, a marina with boat rentals, and swimming permitted in marked zones (no lifeguards, so it's at your own risk). In town there's the Delbert Teets Ball Field and Park, the newer playground and nature trail in Kiowa Park, and Movies in the Park in summer. The Old Trail School, a 1917 schoolhouse on the National Register of Historic Places, serves as the local museum. Bird hunting is a genuine draw out here — A-Plus Game Birds and Longmeadow Game Resort both run pheasant and duck operations nearby.
wiggins.restaurants: Three local places, and that's the honest count: Mariana's Family Restaurant at 612 Central Avenue for Mexican, Just 1 More at 217 Main Street for pizza, burgers and a drink, and High Plains Diner, whose green-chili-smothered breakfast burrito is the thing people order. Anything past that is 15 minutes east in Fort Morgan, or an hour southwest toward Brighton and Denver.
wiggins.dog_parks: No fenced off-leash dog park in Wiggins. Dogs walk on leash at Delbert Teets park and on the Kiowa Park nature trail, and Jackson Lake State Park allows leashed dogs on its shoreline and campground roads. The nearest fenced off-leash parks are Fort Morgan's two, 15 miles east.
wiggins.hikes: There are no mountain trails out here, and no point implying otherwise. The real options are the Kiowa Park nature trail in town, the shoreline and campground loops at Jackson Lake State Park 13 miles north, and Riverside Park's six miles of South Platte river trails in Fort Morgan, 20 minutes east. Foothills trailheads above Boulder and Golden are about an hour and a half southwest.
wiggins.commute: About an hour to Denver on I-76 and under an hour to both Denver International Airport and Greeley — the shortest Front Range commute of any Morgan County town — plus about 15 miles and 20 minutes east to Fort Morgan.
wiggins.relocate_extra: Wiggins is where Morgan County's new construction actually is. Kiowa Park has been built out by a mix of local and regional builders — Baessler Homes, Low Energy Homes, King Family Construction, 2 Valley Builders and Tru-Grit NoCo among them — so a buyer can still find a genuinely new house here at a price that no longer exists in Weld County's I-25 corridor. Two things worth asking before you write an offer: what the water and sewer connection situation is for the specific lot, and how the district is planning for growth, since one campus serves the entire town.

windsor.meta: Welcome to Windsor. In this guide we will explore the local market including listings, schools, businesses, and more.
windsor.welcome: Windsor, Colorado, is a thriving community that blends small-town warmth with modern amenities. Situated between Fort Collins and Greeley, it offers scenic beauty, excellent schools, and a family-friendly atmosphere. With its charming downtown, picturesque parks, and abundant recreational opportunities, Windsor provides a perfect balance of convenience and a high quality of life.
windsor.things_to_do: Enjoy a scenic 2.25-mile trail around Windsor Lake, perfect for walking, biking, or jogging. The lake also offers fishing, boating, and swimming during the warmer months. Step back in time at the Boardwalk Park Museum, featuring seven original historic buildings including a train depot, schoolhouse, and farmhouse. Visit High Hops Brewery to sample a variety of craft beers brewed on-site, alongside its on-site distillery, The Heart Distillery. Golf enthusiasts can enjoy a round at Pelican Lakes Golf Club, known for its extensive lakeside holes along the Poudre River corridor. Explore the Windsor History Museum to learn about the town's rich heritage through exhibits and preserved historic buildings.
windsor.restaurants: Windsor's dining scene mixes local independents with well-loved regional names. Hearth Restaurant and Pub is a local gastropub favorite, while Salathai Windsor is a go-to for Thai standards like drunken noodles and green curry. For breakfast, First Watch draws steady crowds for elevated egg dishes.
windsor.dog_parks: Windsor has two real off-leash options: Poudre Pooch Park, a fenced dog park on the west side of Eastman Park, and a dedicated fenced dog park on the north side of Windsor Lake, with lake access right along the 2.25-mile Windsor Lake Trail.
windsor.hikes: The paved Poudre River Trail runs 21 miles from Windsor to Greeley along the Cache la Poudre River — flat, scenic, and great for a longer walk or bike ride. Fossil Creek Reservoir Natural Area offers a few short trails good for wildlife viewing, and Boyd Lake State Park, just north in Loveland, connects into a larger network of trails.
windsor.commute: About 17 miles / 27 minutes to Fort Collins via CO-14, and about 15 miles / 27 minutes to Greeley via US-34 Business — a genuine dual-commute town.
windsor.relocate_extra: Windsor was Colorado's fastest-growing town among communities of 20,000+ residents, posting 23.3% population growth from April 2020 to July 2023.

pierce.meta: Homes for sale in Pierce, Colorado — a 1,100-person town on US-85 between Greeley and Fort Collins, in the Weld RE-9 Highland district.
pierce.welcome: Pierce is a town of about 1,100 people on US-85, sixteen miles north of Greeley and twenty-one from Fort Collins by way of CO-14. It was incorporated in 1918 and named for General John Pierce, president of the Denver Pacific Railroad, which is the reason a town this size has a Main Street at all. People buy here for the same reason they buy in Ault or Eaton — a real town with a grocery store and a school district, at a price that has not caught up with Fort Collins, and twenty minutes from a job in either direction.
pierce.things_to_do: Pierce is a working agricultural town, not a destination, and the honest version is that most of what you do here is outside or twenty minutes away. What it does have is its own history still standing on Main Street: the old post office, the general store, the mercantile — whose antique shop still opens some days — and the lumber yard. Greeley is sixteen miles south for anything the town does not carry, Fort Collins twenty-one miles west, and the Pawnee National Grassland opens up east of town.
pierce.restaurants: Pierce has a grocery store on Main Street, which matters more than it sounds when the alternative is a sixteen-mile drive for milk. For dining, most people head to Ault a few minutes south, or into Greeley. Rather than name a restaurant that may have changed hands since this page was written, the nearest-restaurant panel above reads live from Google, so it stays current.
pierce.dog_parks: There is no municipal dog park. On most Pierce lots that is beside the point — yards here are generous by Front Range standards, and the town is small enough to walk. If fencing matters to you, it is worth checking what is actually there rather than what the listing photos suggest, because a lot of rural fence line is livestock fence rather than dog-proof.
pierce.hikes: This is plains country, not foothills. The Pawnee National Grassland lies east, with the Pawnee Buttes trail its best-known walk — a genuinely striking one, and quiet almost any day of the year. For mountain trails, people here drive west through Fort Collins to the Poudre Canyon.
pierce.school_district: Weld RE-9 School District (Highland — serving Ault, Pierce, Nunn and Carr)
pierce.commute: 16 miles to Greeley on US-85, and 21 miles to Fort Collins via CO-14. Both are genuine twenty-to-thirty-minute commutes on open road rather than stop-and-go, which is the trade Pierce offers: you drive further and you drive faster. Highland's schools are in Ault, a few minutes south, and Weld RE-9 runs bus routes across 539 square miles.
pierce.relocate_extra: Pierce is small enough that inventory is thin — some months there is very little for sale, and a house that fits you may not be listed the week you start looking. That cuts both ways: it is also why a well-marketed listing here does not sit. Christine has sold three homes in Pierce, including 14775 County Road 88 and two on 4th Street, so she knows what the buyer pool actually looks like and what it pays. If you are looking at acreage outside the town limits, the questions change entirely — wells, septic, water rights, legal access — and those are worth walking the property for before you write an offer.

carr.meta: Land and homes for sale in Carr, Colorado — Weld County acreage near the Wyoming line, halfway between Fort Collins and Cheyenne.
carr.welcome: Carr is an unincorporated community in far northern Weld County, settled in 1872 and sitting almost exactly halfway between Fort Collins and Cheyenne — 32 miles to the first, 22 to the second. Nobody buys in Carr for the town, and it would be strange to pretend otherwise: what is here is a church, the old schoolhouse, a scatter of houses, and land. A great deal of land, with nothing between it and the Front Range but sky. That is the entire proposition, and for the right buyer it is a very good one.
carr.things_to_do: Carr is open country. The Pawnee National Grassland spreads east of here, and the shortgrass prairie in every direction is the reason people come — riding, shooting, hunting, running stock, or simply having no neighbour within sight. The old schoolhouse and the church are what remain of the town proper; the post office closed around 2021 when the building it leased became uninhabitable. For anything else, Fort Collins is 32 miles southwest and Cheyenne 22 miles north — and Cheyenne being that close is a real factor, because Wyoming has no state income tax and plenty of people up here work on one side of the line and live on the other.
carr.restaurants: Being straight about it: Carr has no restaurant and no grocery store. This is the most remote place Christine sells, and eating out means driving — Nunn and Wellington are the nearest small options, Fort Collins and Cheyenne the real ones. The nearest-restaurant and nearest-gas panel above reads live from Google, which for a place like Carr is the single most useful thing on this page.
carr.dog_parks: There is no dog park, and on a Carr parcel the idea is almost funny — the property is the dog park, usually measured in tens of acres. What actually matters here is fencing and whether the fence lines follow the survey, plus the honest question of coyotes, which are a fact of life on the prairie rather than a rare event.
carr.hikes: Not trail country in the foothills sense. The land around Carr is largely private or state trust land rather than public open space, so the walking is on your own ground or in the Pawnee National Grassland to the east, where the Pawnee Buttes trail is the one people drive for. Mountain trails mean going west of Fort Collins.
carr.school_district: Weld RE-9 School District (Highland — serving Ault, Pierce, Nunn and Carr)
carr.commute: 32 miles to Fort Collins and 22 miles to Cheyenne, with I-25 reached via County Road 126. Carr is the closest community to the halfway point between those two cities, which is the practical case for living here: two job markets in two states inside a half-hour each. Be clear-eyed about the school run, though — Highland's schools are in Ault, and Weld RE-9's bus routes cover 539 square miles for a reason.
carr.relocate_extra: Buying in Carr is buying land, and the house is often the smaller half of the decision. Wells and well permits, septic condition, water rights, survey lines, easements and legal access, how far power and fiber actually run, county zoning, and how many animals you may keep and where — every one of those can change what a parcel is worth or whether you can do the thing you bought it for. Many properties out here are USDA-eligible, which can mean no money down, and that comes with its own conditions. Christine has sold acreage in Carr — 54175 County Road 27 among them — and will walk the ground with you asking these questions before you write an offer, not after.
